connectionIntro: Connect to your Thingport instance to import models with one click.
pairNote: Opens Thingport in a tab to approve this browser. Nothing is saved here but the connection it hands back.
pairPending: Finish connecting in the Thingport tab that just opened.
offlineNote: These work without a Thingport instance.
adapt3mfDescription: Adds a Download adapted button to MakerWorld models: a copy for the slicer your Thingport instance opens files in, or without one, the copy PrusaSlicer and the slicers like it read.
darkModeDescription: A dark theme for Thingiverse, which doesn't have one, while your system theme is dark.
hideAdsDescription: Hides the banners, ad cards and video ads on Thingiverse's pages.
viewedEmpty: Models you open on MakerWorld, Printables, Thingiverse and the other sites Grab runs on show up here.
disconnectConfirm: Thingport Grab forgets {host} and its sign-in in this browser. Offline features and recently viewed models stay.
turnOffConfirm: It stops on every site until you turn it back on: no import button, no Download adapted, and Thingiverse looks as it does without Grab. Your connection and settings stay.
invalidInstanceUrl: Enter a valid instance URL, e.g. http://192.168.1.20 or https://thingport.example.com
instancePermission: Thingport Grab needs permission to reach this instance to work.
searchCollection: Search, or type a new name
enablePermission: Thingport Grab needs your browser's permission to run on {site}.
enableAllPermission: Thingport Grab needs your browser's permission to run on these sites.

missingProfilesHint_other: You have {have} of this model's {total} print profiles. Add the {missing} missing as more files on it?

setupIntro: To import from this page, Thingport Grab needs to know where your Thingport instance is, and that instance needs to know this browser:
setupPairHint: Thingport opens in a tab and asks you to approve this browser
setupSecurityHint: Pairing keeps no password in the extension; the setup page still takes an email and password if you'd rather. Either way it's stored only in this browser's extension storage and sent only to your own instance. You can also open this any time from the Thingport Grab icon in your browser toolbar.
setupApprovalRevoked: {instance} no longer accepts this browser's Thingport Grab. It was probably removed from your profile there — pair again.
setupCredentialsRejected: {instance} turned down the email and password saved in Thingport Grab. They were probably changed in Thingport since — sign in again with the current ones.
setupUnreachable: {instance} didn't answer. It may not be running or reachable from this network right now. If it moved, update its URL.
setupOpened: Setup opened in a new tab — you'll be brought back here once it's saved.
setupOpenFailed: Couldn't open setup automatically — click the Thingport Grab icon in your browser toolbar (it may be under the Extensions menu).
scriptSharedShort: The author allows it, so the script comes with the model.
scriptWithheldShort: The author chose not to share the script, so it can't be imported.
scriptSharedExplainer: This model was generated from a script, and its creator shared it — so the script comes along, and you can generate the model again with your own values.
scriptWithheldExplainer: This model was generated from a script, but its creator chose not to share it, so the script can't be imported. The model itself comes over as usual — only customising it again isn't possible.
fabNotSetUp: Thingport Grab isn't set up yet
fabCannotSignIn: Thingport Grab can't sign in to your Thingport instance

collectionProfilesPace: Each print profile is a page visit of its own, after the same wait as a model, to avoid MakerWorld's rate limiting. A run takes about one wait per model and per extra profile.
collectionProfilesExistingPace: Models already in your library are also visited for the print profiles they lack. Each print profile is a page visit of its own, after the same wait as a model, to avoid MakerWorld's rate limiting.

couldNotAdaptMakerworldFile: Couldn't adapt this file: it doesn't look like a 3MF project MakerWorld's Download gives.

couldNotReadMakerworldProfiles: Couldn't read this model's print profiles from its page. Start the import again to carry on: models already brought in are only checked for the profiles they lack.

meshyOwnLocked: Meshy keeps the models its AI agent made for paid plans, even yours.
buyOnMyMiniFactory: Buy it on MyMiniFactory first. Once it's in your library, Thingport imports it from there.
buyOnCgtrader: Buy it on CGTrader first. Once it's in your purchases, Thingport imports it from there.
buyOnCults3d: Buy it on Cults3D first. Once it's in your downloads, Thingport imports it from there.
buyOnThreedexport: Buy it on 3DExport first. Once it's yours, Thingport imports it.

providerAbout.makerworld: Bambu Lab's model site, and the one that put print profiles front and centre: models arrive tuned for a machine and a filament, ready to send to the printer. Designers earn points for them, which buy Bambu gear in its shop.
providerAbout.printables: Prusa Research's repository, called PrusaPrinters until the 2022 rename. It runs several design contests a month and pays contributors in prusameters, points that turn into vouchers for Prusa's own shop.
providerAbout.thingiverse: The original: MakerBot put it up in 2008, and millions of designs later it is still where much of 3D printing's common stock lives, most of it openly licensed. It belongs to UltiMaker now, after MakerBot's merger.
providerAbout.myminifactory: London's iMakr started it in 2013 on a promise: every file test-printed before it went up. It leans heavily on tabletop miniatures, and runs Scan the World, a free archive of scanned sculptures and museum pieces.
providerAbout.snapmaker: Snapmaker's own model site, built around the U1, its multi-colour toolchanger. The company made its name with modular machines that 3D print, laser-cut and carve from one frame.
providerAbout.makeronline: Anycubic's model platform. The company is best known for making resin printing cheap with the Photon, and MakerOnline mixes free and paid models with print profiles and regular designer contests.
providerAbout.crealitycloud: Creality's library and companion app, from the maker of the Ender 3 — the printer that put a 3D printer on most people's first bench. Besides models and profiles it doubles as a remote control for Creality machines.
providerAbout.nexprint: Elegoo's model platform, opened in 2025. Elegoo made its name with the Mars resin printers and the Neptune line, and NexPrint carries profiles for both its own slicer and OrcaSlicer, so models come ready to slice.
providerAbout.thangs: A search engine that matches shapes rather than words: Physna's deep-learning index finds the models geometrically like the one you hand it. It opened in 2020 with a million objects indexed, and sells models now as well.
providerAbout.cults3d: An independent French marketplace for free and paid designs, going since 2014. It sells model by model rather than by subscription, and leans towards figurines, cosplay props and jewellery.
providerAbout.eufymake: Make it Real is the design library of eufyMake — Anker's maker brand, called AnkerMake until 2025. It grew up around the E1 UV printer, whose Kickstarter raised over $44m, more than any project there had before.
providerAbout.pinshape: One of the older community libraries: started in Vancouver in 2013, bought by Formlabs three years on, and run by MatterHackers now. Everything on it is free, and its collections are anyone's to follow.
providerAbout.owlcad: A parametric CAD app that runs in the browser, with a gallery of two halves: a library of CC0 and CC-BY parts to build from, and the projects its users share. Those are CAD, not meshes, so its editor builds the files.
providerAbout.toymakr3d: One designer's shop of articulated robot and mecha models — Transformers, Megazords, Gundams and the like, printed in place with joints that already move. Most are free to download, the rest are sold.
providerAbout.makerables: Makera's project site, where desktop CNC meets 3D printing. Makera makes the Carvera mills, and every project here is free and carries its CAM files and machining programs beside the models they cut.
providerAbout.cgtrader: A Vilnius-born marketplace of over three million 3D models, started in 2011: game and film assets, renders and a large 3D printing catalogue, sold by their designers and many of them free.
providerAbout.grabcad: An engineers' community started in Estonia in 2009 and owned by Stratasys since 2014. Its free library holds millions of CAD models, from machine parts to whole assemblies, mostly as STEP files and native CAD formats.
providerAbout.meshy: An AI 3D model generator that turns a prompt or a picture into a textured model in about a minute. Its community shares the results by the hundred thousand, and lets creators mark the ones fit to print.
providerAbout.pixup3d: Phrozen's 3D model marketplace, from the Taiwanese maker of resin printers. Its designers sell and share figures, busts and tabletop miniatures, many of them pre-supported for resin printing.
providerAbout.fab365: Fab365 is a South Korean 3D-model marketplace, running since 2018. It's known for meticulously engineered models — SpaceX rockets, foldable robots, Star Wars ships — many designed to print cleanly without supports.
providerAbout.threedexport: One of the oldest 3D model marketplaces, open since 2004 and based in San Jose: game and film assets, textures and a large 3D printing catalogue, sold by their designers and some given away free.
adaptedDownloadExplanationUnknown: Your Thingport instance didn't say in time which slicer it opens files in. Grab asks again when you click; if it still can't tell, this downloads the copy PrusaSlicer and the slicers like it read. Made in your browser by Thingport Grab.
adaptedDownloadExplanationCreality: This downloads a copy that keeps the parts, plates, painting and the designer's settings, under the names Creality Print gives them. It still asks which of your printers to use. Made in your browser by Thingport Grab.
adaptedDownloadExplanationBambu: This downloads a copy {slicer} opens as its own project: parts, plates, painting and the designer's settings, without questions about the file's version. A setting it names differently is renamed, to the nearest of its choices where it has fewer. Made in your browser by Thingport Grab.
adaptedDownloadExplanationCura: MakerWorld files are Bambu Studio projects, which Cura opens without their parts' filaments or the designer's settings. This downloads a copy whose multi-part objects keep their parts, each on its own extruder, with the designer's walls, top and bottom layers, infill and whether to print supports set on each object. Cura doesn't read painted colors. Made in your browser by Thingport Grab.
adaptedDownloadExplanationOther: MakerWorld files are Bambu Studio projects, which {slicers} without their colors or print settings. This downloads a copy that goes into your own printer, filament and print settings, with the designer's layer height, walls, infill and supports set on each object and the painted colors on your extruders. Made in your browser by Thingport Grab.
adaptedDownloadOtherSlicers: PrusaSlicer, Cura and other slicers often open
adaptedDownloadOff: Open adapted is off for your slicer in Thingport, so there's no copy to download.
adaptedDownloadNoAnswer: Your Thingport instance didn't answer, so this is the copy PrusaSlicer and the slicers like it read.
adaptedDownloadOriginal: Your slicer opens MakerWorld's files as they are, so this is the file itself.
